name: Miniprep
description: Alkaline lysis miniprep for isolation of plasmid DNA from bacterial cultures. Compatible with most commercial kits (Qiagen QIAprep, Thermo Fisher GeneJET, Zymo Research, etc.).
source_note: General educational template based on alkaline lysis plasmid extraction.

steps.title: Pellet overnight bacterial culture
steps.description: Transfer 1–5 mL of overnight LB bacterial culture to a microcentrifuge tube. Centrifuge to pellet bacteria. Remove supernatant (media) completely.

reagents.name: Overnight E. coli culture in LB+antibiotic

steps.notes: Remove supernatant completely by pipetting or decanting carefully. White cell pellet should be visible.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in Buffer P1 (Resuspension Buffer)
steps.description: Add Buffer P1 to the pellet. Resuspend completely by vortexing or pipetting until no cell clumps remain. Buffer P1 contains RNase A to digest RNA.
steps.notes: Buffer P1 must be stored at 4°C after adding RNase A. Ensure complete resuspension for efficient lysis.

steps.title: Lyse cells with Buffer P2 (Lysis Buffer)
steps.description: Add Buffer P2 (contains NaOH + SDS). Invert gently 4–6 times to mix. The solution will become clear and viscous. Do not vortex. Incubate no longer than 5 minutes.
steps.shakingRotation: Gentle inversion 4–6 times — do NOT vortex
steps.notes: Do NOT vortex — shearing will denature the plasmid. Do not exceed 5 min lysis or gDNA contamination increases.
steps.warnings: SDS is an irritant. Avoid prolonged skin contact.

steps.title: Neutralize with Buffer N3 (or P3)
steps.description: Add Buffer N3 (contains potassium acetate and acetic acid). Mix by inverting 4–6 times until white precipitate forms uniformly. The precipitate contains denatured protein, chromosomal DNA, and SDS.
steps.shakingRotation: Invert 4–6 times until white precipitate is uniform
steps.notes: The solution should turn from clear to cloudy with a white flocculent precipitate. Mixed well if evenly distributed.

steps.title: Centrifuge to clear lysate
steps.description: Centrifuge to pellet the denatured protein/chromosomal DNA precipitate. The clear supernatant contains your plasmid DNA.
steps.notes: Supernatant should be clear. If cloudy, repeat centrifuge. Do not disturb pellet.

steps.title: Load cleared lysate onto spin column
steps.description: Transfer cleared supernatant to the spin column by decanting or pipetting. Centrifuge to bind plasmid DNA to silica membrane. Discard flow-through.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer PE
steps.description: Add wash buffer (PE — ethanol-containing) to the column and centrifuge. Discard flow-through. Perform a dry spin to remove residual ethanol.
steps.centrifugeCondition: 17,900 × g, 1 min; then dry spin 1 min at max
steps.notes: Dry spin removes residual ethanol that would inhibit downstream reactions.

steps.title: Elute plasmid DNA
steps.description: Transfer column to a clean 1.5 mL elution tube. Apply elution buffer (Buffer EB or nuclease-free water) to the center of the membrane. Incubate briefly, then centrifuge.

reagents.name: Buffer EB (elution buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.5) or nuclease-free water

steps.temperature: RT (or pre-warm to 70°C for higher yield)
steps.notes: Eluting with 50 µL gives higher concentration; 100 µL gives higher yield. Pre-warming EB increases yield by ~10–20%.

steps.title: Quantify and verify plasmid
steps.description: Measure DNA concentration using NanoDrop. Expected yield: 5–20 µg per 1.5 mL culture. Verify with agarose gel (should see supercoiled and open-circular bands) and/or restriction digest.
steps.notes: A260/A280 should be ~1.8–1.9. Store at −20°C for long-term storage.
